intended_object: The canonical inclusion morphism 𝓘 ↪ 𝒪_X of sheaves of 𝒪_X-modules, for an ideal sheaf 𝓘 on a scheme X (inferred from the docstring and the module documentation).
explanation: `I.toModule` is the sub-sheaf of 𝒪_X whose sections on each open U are the kernel of 𝒪_X(U) → (ι_* 𝒪_Z)(U), where ι : Z → X is the closed subscheme defined by `I` (built with `unitToPushforwardObjUnit` applied to `I.subschemeι`). This kernel is the ideal sheaf itself: Mathlib states that the kernel of `I.subschemeι` is `I`. `toModuleι` is Mathlib's general `SheafOfModules.Submodule.ι`, the sectionwise subtype inclusion of a sub-sheaf of modules into the ambient sheaf. So the definition is exactly the inclusion 𝓘 → 𝒪_X, in the right setting (ideal sheaves on schemes). Mathlib's IdealSheaf files never mention sheaves of modules, so there is no direct counterpart; this is a specialisation of the general submodule inclusion.
